'''''Star Wars: Shadow of Vader''''' was a planned five-issue [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] miniseries that focused on [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader's]] influence on [[the galaxy]] across eras. Each issue would have followed a different character or group, reflecting on how their encounters with Vader changed their lives.<ref name="Story Info">{{WebCite|url=https://www.kotaku.com.au/2018/10/newstar-wars-books-and-comics-were-announced-at-nycc|text=New Star Wars Books And Comics Were Announced At NYCC|archivedate=20200414135335}}</ref> [[Chuck Wendig]] was originally announced to write the miniseries, but was fired from Marvel in [[October]] [[2018]] after a series of negative and vulgar political tweets attacking [[Wikipedia:Brett Kavanaugh|Brett Kavanaugh]] and the [[Wikipedia:Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]]. According to Wendig at that time, at least issues 4 and 5 of the miniseries weren't going to be written by him anymore.<ref name="Wendig's Firing" />

During New York Comic Con 2018, Wendig told the attendees what each issue would have been about: the first issue was an homage to [[Wikipedia:Friday the 13th (franchise)|''Friday the 13th'']], with Vader hunting down kids at a summer camp; the second issue involved the [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']] background character [[Willrow Hood]]; the third issue centered on a morgue attendant on the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[battle station]]; the fourth issue diverged to focus on the [[Acolytes of the Beyond]], first seen in Wendig's [[Star Wars: The Aftermath Trilogy|''The Aftermath Trilogy'']]; and the fifth issue followed a [[New Republic]] [[pilot]]—whose parents were [[Death|killed]] by Vader—who joins the [[Resistance]] only to learn that [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa's]] [[Parent|father]] was none other than Vader himself.<ref name="NYCC" />

The series was to be published by [[Marvel Comics]] starting [[November]] [[2018]],<ref name="NYCC" /> but was delayed until [[February]] [[2019]] as it wasn't mentioned in January's solicitations.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://comicbook.com/starwars/news/star-wars-shadow-of-vader-chuck-wendig-fired-marvel-delayed|text=Chuck Wendig's 'Shadow of Vader' Star Wars Series Has Been Pulled From Marvel's Schedule|author=Schmidt, J.K.|date=2018-10-17|work=ComicBook.com|archivedate=20200920140504}}</ref><ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/fired-marvel-writer-chuck-wendigs-shadow-vader-series-pulled-1153061|text=The five-part comic book series is absent from the company's January 2019 releases.|author=McMillan, Graeme|date=2018-10-17|work=The Hollywood Reporter|archivedate=20181017214709}}</ref> Wendig later speculated at his [[Wikipedia:Twitter|Twitter]] account that perhaps Marvel would hire a new writer to rewrite the first three issues or that the series has been cancelled.<ref name="Ultimate Fate of Shadow?">{{Twitter|ChuckWendig|status/1052526172393926657|Chuck Wendig|quote=Also possible they are looking for a brand new writer on the first three issues OR they just said fuck it, and canceled it quietly. Obviously, ha ha, they're not gonna keep me on the loop on that one.}}</ref> On [[November 15]], 2018, however, Marvel officially confirmed via [[Wikipedia:Bleeding Cool|Bleeding Cool]] that the series had effectively been cancelled.<ref name="Cancellation">{{WebCite|url=https://www.bleedingcool.com/2018/11/15/marvel-cancels-star-wars-shadow-of-vader-chuck-wendig|text=Marvel Cancels All Of Star Wars: Shadow Of Vader by Chuck Wendig|author=Johnston, Rich|date=2018-11-15|work=[[Wikipedia:Bleeding Cool|Bleeding Cool]]|archivedate=20190611220331}}</ref>
